sources.citation: Moe, Jonathan. 2023. A phonology of the Domung [dev] language of Papua New Guinea with acoustic analysis. MA thesis (Linguistics), Trinity Western University / Canada Institute of Linguistics. xi+c.170 pp.
sources.note: No Madi/Gira data or statement. Value is negative evidence: a 2023 SIL-PNG-insider census of Finisterre phonological descriptions has no entry for Madi/Gira, confirming that no OPD or Phonology Essentials paper exists for it; the nearest described relatives (Nekgini, Ngaing, Iyo) disagree among themselves on accent (non-contrastive / lexical / penultimate), so no family-level inference is safe.

sources.citation: Sarvasy, Hannah. 2014. Four Finisterre-Huon languages: An introduction. STUF - Language Typology and Universals 67(3). doi:10.1515/stuf-2014-0017
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Family-level typological introduction; would give at most a general Finisterre-Huon stress remark, nothing Gira-specific expected.
Stub; bibliography = Cicero 1995 wordlist (SIL-PNG archive 67612) and Claassen & McElhanon 1970 p. 50.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarstrom. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Nothing on Madi. Family-level secondhand remark in the phonology section (p. 89 of the chapter, after Ross 2005): 'In languages of the Madang and Finisterre-Huon groups and of South-east Papua generally, tone and pitch accent are largely absent.' Also 'In Finisterre-Huon languages it is common to find seven vowels'. Not a statement about this languoid; recorded as context only.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: No phonology content: census/classification inventory (speaker numbers, village lists, sources 'Claassen-McElhanon 1970', interrogative 'what' forms per language). No stress/accent/tone remarks for any Finisterre language.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. Canberra: ANU.
sources.harvard_location: Divinity School Library (offsite storage), call number - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354 .Z91
sources.note: Gira appears only in the language list and a pronoun table; the phonology section (10 representative languages) contains no stress/accent statement at all (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11, 45-78. Pacific Linguistics A-23. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A23.45 (sealang.net/archives/pl/pdf/)
sources.note: Nothing for Gira. Sec. 2.1.1 (p. 50) gives only location (coast west of Saidor, Mot census division), c. 400 speakers, dialects Yeimas/Wab. Sec. 6.1 Phonology treats one representative language per family (Rawa for Gusap-Mot), segment inventories only; the paper's sole stress remark is note 11 on Wantoat (Davis 1967: stress non-phonemic).

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1970. The Trans-New Guinea Phylum: Explorations in deep-level genetic relationships. Pacific Linguistics B-16. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Printed source of the Gira comparative wordlist reproduced on TransNewGuinea.org; check whether the original transcription marks stress (the online copy does not).

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1970. The Selepet language within the Finisterre-Huon phylum (New Guinea). PhD thesis, Australian National University, Canberra. 487 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Gira: the name occurs once (language list). Text-layer search for stress/accent/tone/tonal/pitch finds no prosodic statement in the comparative chapters (only Wurm 1954 'Tonal languages in New Guinea' in the bibliography); Selepet-specific phonology is out of scope here.

sources.citation: Schmitz, Carl A. 1959. Zur Ethnologie der Rai-Kuste in Neuguinea. Anthropos 54: 27-56.
sources.note: No phonology content: enumerates language groups by village and explicitly defers the linguistic structure of the Finisterre/Saruwaged hinterland to a separate publication (Schmitz 1960); the rest is social organisation, cults, migration history.
